text:
noah: quick flag 1: our SSE->WS fallback patch rolled to canary in ap-south and we're seeing a tight reconnect loop in a subset of mobile clients. console shows socket_close spikes but no matching streaming.events due to sampling + early-proxy short-circuit.

mai: which patch? the graceful-fallback or the new sticky-route header?

noah: graceful-fallback v2 with sticky-route header `x-sticky-route`. timeline: deploy 12:03 -> spike 12:07. logs show a pattern: proxy accepts ws, immediately sends `101` then client reconnects within 50-200ms repeatedly.

reve: could be mobile NAT hairpin or aggressive app retry backoffs. do we have tenant breakdown?

noah: yep, concentrated on tenant "edu-apps" in ap-south. sample trace: 

```
12:07:01 conn=zz99 route=ap-south tenant=edu-apps event=upgrade 101
12:07:01 conn=zz99 event=close reason=client.reset
12:07:01 reconnect attempt backoff=0.2s
12:07:02 conn=zz99 route=ap-south sampled=false stream.event=closed
```

noah: note sampled=false again.

deploy-bot: deploy 1799994400 applied to service/gateway-canary at 12:03:12 by ci-cd

mai: recurring theme: sampling for high-volume streaming is low by default. canary traffic is too small and gets filtered. this makes rollouts blind.

reve: two things we should do immediately: (A) emit a low-cardinality `stream.fallback_probe=1` on upgrade/fallback paths and mark `telemetry_only=true`, (B) for requests with header `x-rollout-candidate: yes` set metrics.sampling.rate=1 for 10m.

noah: also propose to add a tiny jitter to the client-side retry (sdk change) and server-side accept backoff so we don't thundering-herd. sdk patch would be non-breaking: random(50ms,250ms) added to retry.

console-team: dashboard asks: show probe counts side-by-side with socket_close so on-call can see mismatch. add a sample_fraction indicator.

mai: operational rule: if socket_close_rate > 100/min and probe_count < 40 in 5m for a canary, auto-pause rollout. otherwise continue and keep sampling override for 30m.

reve: caution: `rollout_id` tag increases cardinality; only emit it when header present and only for canary. also probes must not be billed or counted against quota.

noah: implementation sketch: 
```
# in proxy
if req.headers['x-rollout-candidate']=='yes':
  metrics.sampling.override = 1.0
  metrics.emit('stream.fallback_probe', tags={'telemetry_only':'true', 'rollout_id': req.headers.get('x-rollout-id','canary-1799994400')})
else:
  if fallback_path: metrics.emit('stream.fallback_probe', tags={'telemetry_only':'true'})
```

reve: small ask: make the probe metric low-cardinality (boolean tags) and strip tenant IDs. console can join on tenant using aggregation layers.

deploy-bot: incident created: INC-2299 "canary: websocket fallback reconnect loop - missing telemetry" assigned to @noah priority=P2

mai: quick UX note: console should surface a warning pill during rollouts: "Telemetry may be sampled; enable rollout filter to see full events" and link to runbook. reduces messy P1 escalations.

noah: will open PRs for proxy probe + sampling override and sdk jitter. will coordinate with console for panel.

reve: action items: 1) sampling override applied now for canary header, 2) emit probe from proxy, 3) sdk jitter patch in next 2h, 4) add dashboard card and rollout-warning banner, 5) add auto-pause rule in rollout controller.

mai: timeline acked. thanks y'all. :thumbsup: leaving thread for async updates.
